# Prototype dictionary provenance

These data retain their original licenses. Neither upstream checker implementation is imported.

## Current local data — 2026-09-12

The Worker now uses Open Korean Text and MeCab selected data under Apache-2.0, plus the pinned Wordnik wordlist and Wonboard original basic forms under MIT. The generator, review dialog and combined notices have been updated together. English contains 198,499 entries; Korean complete-word recognition adds the predicate-stem fields reviewed below. Combined gzip size is 1,861,303 bytes. Current lexicon SHA-256: `582a81dcf351da3b369eb4d7cb4b8f3410612dadf60ded14f35af74ffd8000cc`.

The September 12 morphology increment selects Hangul surfaces with the expected VV/VA/VX part of speech and exact 12-field layout from the same pinned MeCab revision's `VV.csv`, `VA.csv`, and `VX.csv`. Source hashes match the prior isolated acquisition: `2929d7cfd45c30d64bfe2b8e6e31f6362772c95a7e2646968a10df04116f60d2`, `5508849ef6054533ffe1e81a8c2351838e538e98ba62a9f97a09836f2f19dbab`, and `b8168dcdf7bcb0d7aadbd91b5372f24bfd5d4908f631a561f31e4945daf0a543`. The pinned repository COPYING was retrieved again and matches the retained Apache-2.0 notice byte for byte. The 7,357 verb/auxiliary and 2,355 adjective surfaces are complete-word recognition inputs, not additions to the spacing-fragment vocabulary or edit-distance candidates. Existing forms, adverbs, recognition nouns, action nouns and state-change nouns are byte-equivalent when serialized field by field. The morphology payload SHA-256 before the geographic-name increment was `6c7f2a1e45e8eb522a6efa79915e5a9748a8a1c484cb252c447fcfdad81b12be`. No MeCab implementation, cost table, connection IDs, external definitions, private corpus text or additional source license is included. The modified-data notice is retained in the payload; the original COPYING and public combined notice remain unchanged. These statements establish the reviewed incremental provenance, not linguistic correctness.

The September 13 geographic-name increment selects 30,240 unique Hangul surfaces of 2–20 characters from `Place.csv` at the same pinned MeCab revision `12439fb32808b9244ded56d7dfed96e4b8d76869`, requiring 12 fields, NNP and the geographic semantic tag. The generated manifest records the source URL, hash and byte count. These names recognize complete nominals with bounded particle/copula tails only; they do not enter segmentation fragments, spelling candidates or productive predicate roots. All prior payload fields other than the modified-data notice remain unchanged. COPYING was fetched from that revision again and is byte-identical to the retained Apache-2.0 license. The current morphology SHA-256 is `38a8386eace92d1e1ecff9c9a2f2c40989c851651305511f537314885d9f257a`. No implementation, cost/connection data or private corpus text is included. The combined compressed dictionaries remain below the existing 2,000,000-byte cap. This provenance check does not establish linguistic completeness.

The September 11 increment adds only the authored `AHK` acronym to `englishBasicForms()`, corroborated by AutoHotkey's official project name and script extension at https://github.com/AutoHotkey/Ahk2Exe. No upstream implementation, dictionary, definition or sentence was copied. Removing this one entry and serializing identically reproduces the prior reviewed SHA-256 `3a2beebd42cbab39bbb3f7c81d90327dca4398476cb293cd9154045204c76b54`; Korean lists, all other English entries and notice text are unchanged. The original enumeration remains Wonboard MIT. This audit establishes the provenance of the incremental bytes, not broad name coverage.

`node scripts/check-spelling-data-policy.mjs` checks the reviewed payloads and original notices. Passing this narrow license-policy check is not release approval or linguistic accuracy certification. The replacement passed isolated Worker performance and 51 existing UI tests before local promotion. Independent language-quality qualification remains incomplete. No deployment was performed. Historical SCOWL notice files are retained for earlier revisions, but are no longer imported by the Worker UI or notices builder.

The `build`, `build:sites`, and `build:desktop` package scripts now run this check before compilation and stop on failure. Direct tool invocations such as `vite build` bypass these package scripts. Packaging an already-built desktop app does not requalify its existing output. Use the documented build command first; this gate checks source data, not the freshness of a packaged artifact.

## Historical audit before local replacement

The following records describe the earlier ESDB payload and candidate investigation, not the current local imports. Present-tense restrictions and commands below are historical snapshots; the current state and build gate are described above.

## Release restriction: strict MIT / Apache-2.0 policy

The current combined `generated/lexicon.json` is **not approved for release under the requested allowlist**. It contains 114,496 English entries extracted from ESDB/SCOWL under its own permission notice, not MIT or Apache-2.0. Keeping that notice does not make the asset satisfy the narrower project requirement. This is a policy mismatch, not a claim that ESDB forbids redistribution.

The existing builder downloads that source and the notices builder includes it. Do not describe the combined payload as MIT/Apache-only. No dictionary has been removed or replaced as part of this audit; English functionality remains experimental until an eligible replacement is verified or the user explicitly changes the policy.

Local preflight: `node scripts/check-spelling-data-policy.mjs`. It compares the two current payloads and their retained notices to the reviewed hashes, then checks the explicit license allowlist. The current result must be exit 1 for `LicenseRef-ESDB`. A changed file also fails until its provenance is reviewed again. This check neither determines copyright ownership nor measures spelling quality, and is not yet wired into release/build automation. Run it before considering a release; a normal build succeeding does not establish policy compliance.

Candidate checked: `https://github.com/mastermunj/english-lexicon` advertises MIT, but its documented inputs include SCOWL and Wikipedia word frequency. Its repository badge alone does not establish an eligible replacement. No data from it was imported. `https://github.com/wooorm/dictionaries` likewise requires per-dictionary license review; the wrapper license is not evidence for its word lists.

To close this restriction, verify the replacement data's own license and provenance, update the generator and retained notices, regenerate the payload, and rerun both spelling accuracy and normal-expression preservation tests. Deleting English support or relabeling the existing payload is not an approved substitute.

### Additional candidate: Wordnik wordlist

`node scripts/stage-proofreading-bundle.mjs` stages the full candidate data pair for Worker testing, not only the English list. It verifies the reviewed source payloads and Korean notices, retains the existing Korean data unchanged, and substitutes only the staged MIT English list. The new temporary directory includes both payloads and the original notices. Current combined gzip size is 1,688,550 bytes (under the 2,000,000-byte data limit); staged lexicon SHA-256 is `670827c8b969235c00a29fd6a2c84ab9c714b02e492a7078c7234c498a800037`. This is not a production import change or release qualification. Runtime and language-quality checks remain required.

The isolated generator also emits `english-with-basics.json` (198,498 entries, SHA-256 `ec831bcbb0ea48479e7293845c9b677dc1dfe2d5bc4974d0bbb72c37e9cf0a44`). The 76 added forms are an original enumeration in `scripts/english-basic-forms.mjs`, not an extraction from SCOWL: basic contractions, days/months, and a few abbreviations. Its manifest enumerates every added form and retains Wonboard's MIT notice separately. The raw candidate remains unchanged for comparison. This small supplement is not complete grammatical coverage and does not solve candidate ranking or proper-name recognition.

Reproducible isolated preparation: `node scripts/stage-wordnik-candidate.mjs`. The script verifies revision `46e6215d0f90356afe9c8ba4be347e7e98cb425c`, the word-list hash below, and the original MIT notice hash `a568f0ac4c7ad5248ff748387d41e39519811b4a3e07d7438c9d1465dd4c9339`. It creates a new temporary directory containing English-only JSON, the unchanged license notice, and a provenance manifest. It never updates production assets. The generated payload has 198,422 entries and SHA-256 `13f387f9bf8096a1538eb57127d7d01a8e3ba70614c19b423108ef10367059fc`. Quality qualification, grammatical supplementation and ranking remain open; the release restriction above still applies.

On 2026-09-10, read the publisher-maintained `https://github.com/wordnik/wordlist`, its README and LICENSE. The repository's primary artifact is the word list itself, and its LICENSE declares MIT with copyright 2020 Wordnik. The README identifies a word-game vocabulary and separately offers richer data under a paid license; that paid dataset was not accessed. This is a stronger eligible-data candidate than a wrapper carrying an unrelated upstream dictionary, but is not yet an approved product replacement.

An in-memory probe fetched `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wordnik/wordlist/main/wordlist-20210729.txt`: 2,366,872 bytes, SHA-256 `bfd1b4eb4ade1ba81e84c7e24248b9a1aecec9d9baa427453b367a83e30e0451`, 198,422 lowercase alphabetic entries. This mutable URL must be replaced with a verified commit pin before any distribution. No fetched words were written into the repository or substituted in the production bundle.

Only 79,402 of the existing 114,496 English entries overlapped exactly; that is a coverage comparison, not an accuracy result. With the current checker, ordinary `I` and `a` were flagged, API and USB were unrecognized, and `teh` ranked `eth` before `the`. `recieve`, `definately` and `accomodation` did include useful corrections. Word-game coverage and lexical ranking need separate evaluation, including contractions, capitalized names, abbreviations and common-word preference. Retain the existing release restriction until the complete replacement and its tests are approved; do not treat an MIT declaration alone as product qualification.

* Open Korean Text: `https://github.com/open-korean-text/open-korean-text`, revision `74cc4ae7d3dab232747cd5ddb723e4b73c476e4f`. Original `LICENSE` saved here (11325 bytes). Apache-2.0; preserve license and mark transformations. Recursive tree inspection found no NOTICE file. Only basic noun/adverb/adjective/verb/josa/eomi text lists are selected; Wikipedia-derived and other thematic lists are excluded.
* English Speller Database (formerly SCOWL): `https://github.com/en-wl/wordlist`, revision `1e5b7d3a72f47a71da5d28686c1dd4b397178485`. Original `Copyright` saved here (4903 bytes), including all component notices. The permission grants redistribution and modification of generated word lists with notices; no checker code is imported. Recursive tree inspection found no separate NOTICE file. SCOWL 2020 was inspected but not acquired or used.

* MeCab Ko Dic (data only): `https://github.com/lindera/mecab-ko-dic`, revision `12439fb32808b9244ded56d7dfed96e4b8d76869`. Apache-2.0 license is retained in `mecab-ko-dic/COPYING`. Selected fields from Inflect.csv, MAG.csv, NNG.csv and Foreign.csv; costs and engine IDs are removed. Common and foreign nouns supplement whole-word recognition only, not segmentation candidates or spelling-candidate generation. Dictionary membership does not override explicit spelling rules. No MeCab engine code is included.

Source URLs, sizes and hashes are in generated manifests. Source JSON lives outside public/ but is now bundled into the experimental review Worker; it is therefore a distributed resource, not an unshipped prototype. Notices are available in the review dialog and public/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt. Existing released checker assets and their historical notices remain until the replacement quality gate passes; they are not a fallback for the new Worker.
# Noun derivation subsets

`generated/morphology.json` includes `actionNouns`, selected from the pinned MeCab NNG.csv rows classified as 행위 (2–20 Hangul syllables). Wonboard uses this subset for -하다 and -되다 derivation recognition and context-sensitive -하다 spacing review. `stateChangeNouns` selects the same source's 상태변화 class with the same surface filter, and supplements only -되다 derivation. These Apache-2.0 data retain the same source hash and COPYING notice in the manifest. Neither subset expands general noun spelling candidates. A semantic class is not a guarantee that every generated expression is standard Korean.

### Recognition-only static-state nouns

The current payload also retains 2,708 `정적사태` surfaces as `recognitionStaticStateNouns` from the same pinned NNG.csv. Only the separate whole-word recognizer receives this set for noun-derived 하다 forms. General segmentation and spelling-candidate vocabularies remain unchanged. The isolated development experiment removed two wrong suggestions without losing a correct one; this is not a certification that every derivation is standard. All seven prior fields were compared equal with the preceding snapshot, and all seven downloaded source hashes matched the retained local acquisition. The reviewed payload SHA-256 is `6c7f2a1e45e8eb522a6efa79915e5a9748a8a1c484cb252c447fcfdad81b12be`; both data payloads total 1,733,088 gzip bytes. Original COPYING and license terms are unchanged.
